ZWE.note: Only an online application platform for passports and ID cards is announced; no authentication service is stated.
The population registry's link to hospitals is for registering births and deaths; no link between the civil register and the ID system is stated.

facts.fact: Registrar-General Henry Machiri said the Civil Registry Department had computerised civil registration stations at all provinces and some districts and sub-offices, was rolling computerisation out to the remaining sub-offices, and was linking the ZPRS database to hospitals for instant registration of births and deaths.

ZWE.note: No enrolment count or share is stated.
No number at birth is stated.
Nothing on who builds, maintains or owns the system beyond the department issuing cards.
Linking to hospitals is stated, but no public register keyed on the ID number.

facts.fact: Registrar-General Henry Machiri said the Civil Registry Department was issuing national ID cards from computerised offices, with machines each able to produce at least 200 cards a day, and that the ZPRS database holds each individual's national ID number.

The Herald reports ZPRS is the official platform that stores and manages demographic data of all Zimbabwean citizens, including name, date of birth, sex, nationality, marital status, place of birth and residence, and national ID number, with an upgrade being finalised.

ZWE.note: Offices are said to be computerised but the document names no event entered digitally at registration and gives no share of offices.
